messages.subject: Difference in value of derived parameter output depending on method
parts:
Dear forum

I seek your help regarding an apparent discrepancy (most likely the result of a blatant mistake on my behalf) in derived parameter outputs using two different methods. In terms of background, I am running a multi-season (a total of 16 surveys made up of four surveys per year over four years) single species (black rats) site occupancy analysis. 30 cameras were consistently set for at least 22 nights per season.

I have constructed the unmarkedmulti-frame, including a number of different types of covariates, and the summary of the unmarked multi-frame makes sense. I am running models using the colext function and they have been converging etc with no error messages.  When it comes to estimating changes in prob of site occupancy (psi) across seasons, I have attempted using two different methods. The first is manual derivation e.g.

T<-16

psi<-rep(NA,T)

psi[1]<-0.7910741 #obtained using predict for the relevant model

gamma<-0.2955872 #obtained using predict for the relevant model

epsilon<-0.2471236 #obtained using predict for the relevant model

phi<-1-epsilon

Z<-rep(NA,T)

Z[1] <- rbinom(1, 1, psi)

for(t in 2:T) {

  psi[t] <- psi[t-1]*phi + (1-psi[t-1])*gamma

   Z[t] <- rbinom(1, 1, Z[t-1]*phi + (1-Z[t-1])*gamma)

  }

psi

 

And the second method is nonparametric bootstrapping e.g.

mymodel <- nonparboot(mymodel, B = 100)

cbind(smoothed=smoothed(mymodel)[2,], SE=mymodel_at_smoothed.mean.bsse[2,])

 

The first estimate of psi is the same between the two methods, however subsequent estimates for psi for the remaining seasons are different. I am reasonably confident that the estimates arising from the nonparboot method are accurate, however I need to make sure given the two different outputs. Can someone please clarify that the code I have used for the nonparboot is correct in this case? And also if anyone has a neat add on section of code for the nonparboot method to compute 95% confidence intervals in addition to standard error that would be very much appreciated.
PS I exchanged the @ in the last line of command for _at_  given the line command was being mistaken for an email address. 

Kind regards, Bill.
